facts.fact_text: On 5 May 2018 people assembled into a non-approved rally in Cheboksary.
The non-approved rally on 5 May 2018 was held in a different manner as compared to the notice lodged by Ms P.
At 2 p.m. on 5 May 2018 at Respublika Square in Cheboksary, according to the applicants, the police ordered the demonstrators to cease the meeting.
According to the applicants, the police threatened the demonstrators at Respublika Square with use of force when ordering them to cease the meeting.
After the police order at Respublika Square, the demonstrators started to move through the main town streets of Cheboksary, walking on the pavements to avoid disruption of traffic.
The demonstrators moving through the main town streets of Cheboksary were followed by the police.
At Chapayev Square in Cheboksary, the demonstrators were met by another police squad and dispersed.
According to the authorities, the applicants did not comply with the police order to cease participation in the meeting at Respublika Square on 5 May 2018.
According to the authorities, from 2.30 to 4 p.m. on 5 May 2018, the applicants participated in an event at Chapayev Square in Cheboksary.
The authorities and the courts classified the event at Chapayev Square on 5 May 2018 as a "demonstration" under the Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act).
According to the authorities, the applicants did not comply with the police order to cease participation in the demonstration at Chapayev Square on 5 May 2018.

Pursuant to sections 5 and 7 of the Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act), the organiser of a public event must notify the executive or municipal authority of the event.
Under the Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act), the procedure for notification of a public event is determined by a regional statute.

Under the Chuvashiya Republic's Statute no. 77 of 30 November 2012, public events were prohibited at all locations mentioned in section 8 of the Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act).
Under the Chuvashiya Republic's Statute no. 77 of 30 November 2012, public events were prohibited at or near shopping malls or markets and within fifty metres of them.

Under the Chuvashiya Republic's Statute no. 77 of 30 November 2012, public events were prohibited at buildings hosting educational, children-related, cultural, medical or sports institutions and, until 2020, within fifty metres of those buildings.
Under the Chuvashiya Republic's Statute no. 77 of 30 November 2012, public events were prohibited at sports areas and children's playgrounds.
Under the Chuvashiya Republic's Statute no. 77 of 30 November 2012, public events were prohibited at religious buildings or objects and, until 2020, within fifty metres of them.
Under the Chuvashiya Republic's Statute no. 77 of 30 November 2012, public events were prohibited at buildings hosting municipal and public authorities and, until 2020, within thirty metres of them.
Under the Chuvashiya Republic's Statute no. 77 of 30 November 2012, public events were prohibited at entrances to residential buildings if the distance was less than five metres.
The Supreme Court of the Chuvashiya Republic found that Mr Ryabenko had committed a serious breach of public order and public safety in relation to the demonstration on 5 May 2018.

The Supreme Court of the Chuvashiya Republic found that Mr Ryabenko's actions had entailed consequences consisting of the presence of numerous people on the pavements in the town centre of Cheboksary and near buildings hosting public authorities.

The Supreme Court of the Chuvashiya Republic found that Mr Ryabenko's actions had impeded the movement of pedestrians and had created a real threat of interfering with the authorities' functioning and other people's rights.
The Cheboksary town administration informed Ms P. that the itinerary for the march included areas where public events were not allowed under the regional legislation.
The specially designated area proposed by the Cheboksary town administration was specifically at Sosnovskaya Street, next to a church, a local police station and a children's park.
According to the applicants, the distance between the venue proposed by the Cheboksary town administration and the initially proposed venue amounted to some fifty kilometres.

According to the applicants, the venue proposed by the Cheboksary town administration had poor transport and public infrastructure which would have been impracticable for the presence of hundreds of participants.
